clue.text: Husband, prepared for battle, getting wounded

parts.note: troops carrying weapons and ready to fight are armed

explanation.surface: A husband, kitted out for war, comes home injured.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to be harmed is to be hurt or injured.

clue.text: Important person gets recently stolen goods

definitions.meaning: someone impressive or highly capable is called this informally
stolen goods still sought by police are 'hot'

explanation.surface: A big shot is caught with freshly nicked loot.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an impressive person, and loot that is still too risky to sell.

clue.text: Maybe sister Joy follows brother ultimately

indicators.note: follows puts joy after the brother's last letter
ultimately points to the final letter of brother

parts.note: elation is great joy

explanation.surface: A sister's happiness comes after her brother's in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A sister is an example of a family member, so 'maybe' marks it as one instance.

clue.text: Woman making some men idiotic

indicators.note: making some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A woman who makes some men act foolishly.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, as in Enid Blyton, so an example of a woman.

clue.text: One church certain to be cut off in bad weather

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
CE is short for Church of England
bound, as in 'bound to happen', means certain

explanation.surface: A lone church is sure to be isolated when the weather turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship or settlement locked in by frozen water is stranded until the thaw, isolated by winter conditions.

clue.text: Study to get trophy — is bit of money making one passionate?

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
a cup is a sporting trophy
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: Swotting for a prize and a little cash stirs someone's ardour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means full of strong sexual desire, i.e. lustful.

clue.text: Buy teapots specially made in idyllic location

indicators.note: something specially made is put together afresh, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Bespoke teapots are on sale in a lovely spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenic place of natural loveliness that draws visitors.

clue.text: Less attractive gruel, horrible for one to tuck into

indicators.note: to tuck into puts the letter for one inside the jumble
horrible suggests the gruel is a mess, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Nasty gruel for one person to eat looks even worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' rearranges GRUEL into UGLER, and 'to tuck into' sets I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of the adjective for unsightly.

clue.text: Medical problem declines with ending of puberty

parts.note: something that falls or decreases drops

indicators.note: ending of picks out the final letter of puberty

explanation.surface: A health complaint fades as adolescence ends.
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for oedema, swelling caused by fluid in the body tissue.

clue.text: Drunkard appears after start of the film

indicators.note: appears after places the drunkard behind the opening letter
start of picks out only the opening letter of the word the

parts.note: an alkie is slang for an alcoholic

explanation.surface: A drunk turns up just as the film begins.
explanation.definitionFit: An early motion picture with a soundtrack, as opposed to a silent one, was called by this name.

clue.text: Toiling with difficulty to incorporate a design

indicators.note: to incorporate means the anagram takes the letter a inside it
doing something with difficulty suggests the letters of toiling are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone labours hard to work a pattern into something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toiling' looks like the surface's verb but is the fodder; an intaglio is a design cut into a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraved or carved figure cut into a gem or stone surface is a kind of decorative pattern.

clue.text: American clubs maybe first to sponsor places for posh passengers

parts.note: clubs is one of four suits, so a fourth part of what Americans call a deck of cards

indicators.note: first to points at the opening letter of sponsor

explanation.surface: A US club funds seating for wealthy travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: Clubs is one quarter of a pack of cards, which in American usage is a deck; 'maybe' marks clubs as just one suit.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear upper deck of a ship, traditionally reserved for officers and important passengers.

clue.text: Monkey, one following bird

indicators.note: following puts the letter for one behind the bird

parts.note: the tit is a small songbird
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A monkey trails along behind a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A small South American primate of the genus Callicebus goes by this name.

clue.text: Noble quality of head following holiday time?

indicators.note: following puts the head after the holiday month

parts.note: August is the main summer holiday month in Britain, hence the question mark
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Fife Ness

explanation.surface: A dignified air comes over someone's head once the holidays are over.
explanation.walkthrough: NESS is a headland, a promontory, found in place names such as Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Being august means being majestic and dignified, so the noun names that stately character.

clue.text: Welcome offer from fishmonger who is not normally generous type?

definitions.text: Welcome offer from fishmonger who is not normally generous type?

parts.words: Welcome offer from fishmonger who is not normally generous type?
parts.note: a stingy fishmonger's rare bargain would be a fish sold at a low price, and that phrase also names a miser

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted fishmonger surprises everyone with a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words it is a low-priced ray-like fish, the welcome offer; read as one word it names a stingy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for a miserly person who avoids spending money.

clue.text: Treat self to hairdo that is most bold and stupid

indicators.note: to treat something is to work on it, so these letters are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: Pampering yourself with a new haircut is the most reckless thing you could do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treat' rearranges the twelve letters of SELF TO HAIRDO.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of the adjective for rash, recklessly daring behaviour.

clue.text: Point in space could appear to be a pinhole

indicators.note: could appear to be suggests the letters of a pinhole take on another form

explanation.surface: A spot in the night sky might look like a tiny hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could appear to be' rearranges A PINHOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The position in a planet's orbit farthest from the sun, a location in the heavens.

clue.text: Professional words in religious book

parts.note: pro is short for professional
verbs are words of one grammatical class

explanation.surface: An expert's language appears in a sacred text.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of the Old Testament, so an example of a scriptural volume.

clue.text: Arrived with a mower and had an accident

parts.note: came is the past tense of come, so arrived
something that crops grass is a cropper

explanation.surface: Someone turned up with a lawnmower and then had a mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: To come a cropper is a British idiom for falling heavily or failing badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for taking a bad fall or suffering a sudden mishap.

clue.text: Attending university hospital, unwell — struggle being this?

parts.note: in British usage a student is 'up' at university
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A sick student in the university hospital finds life hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition completes the phrase 'an uphill struggle', a hard slog.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a laborious task is described with this adjective, like climbing a slope.

clue.text: Cold person seen as victim becomes more intimate

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
a loser is someone who always comes off worst

explanation.surface: A chilly underdog warms to someone and gets friendlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of the adjective for intimate, as in friends who are near.

clue.text: Putting a fence around land a pig is wandering about

indicators.note: letters wandering about move freely and end up in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is enclosing the land because a pig keeps roaming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering about' rearranges LAND A PIG IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A palisade is a fence of stakes, so the verb form means enclosing ground with one.

clue.text: Fuel carried by wider vehicles

indicators.note: carried by says the letters travel inside the words wider vehicles

explanation.surface: Wide lorries carry their fuel load.
explanation.walkthrough: DERV is the British name for diesel used in road vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel oil for road vehicles, from 'diesel-engined road vehicle'.

clue.text: Sweetheart demanding on the purse

definitions.meaning: a term of endearment for a loved one

explanation.surface: A girlfriend who costs a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word serves as an endearment for a loved one and as a word for high-priced.

clue.text: Legal act keeps children outside political party

indicators.note: outside says the children wrap round the party

parts.note: issue is a legal word for offspring
the ANC is the African National Congress of South Africa

explanation.surface: A law keeps kids away from party politics.
explanation.definitionFit: The formal putting out of a writ, licence or document is an official act of authority.

clue.text: Strong suit of this writer, wild beast with no heart

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as this writer, giving me

indicators.note: with no heart says the central letter of the beast is removed

parts.note: a tiger is a wild big cat

explanation.surface: The writer's speciality is a fierce animal, minus its heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no heart' takes G from the middle of TIGER, leaving TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's forte or line of work they excel at is their calling.

clue.text: Generosity of spirit and less rage somehow needed

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of less rage are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: Being big-hearted requires a little less anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: liberal giving and open-handed bounty.

clue.text: Shrubs giving their audible instruction to gardener when too big!

indicators.note: audible says the shrubs' words are heard, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.words: instruction to gardener when too big
parts.note: overgrown bushes would ask the gardener to 'prune us'

explanation.surface: Overgrown bushes call out to the gardener to cut them back.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant genus including plums, cherries and blackthorn, many grown as ornamental bushes.
